newsitem.title: UK: Branson sees second balloon trip, then maybe space.
newsitem.headline: Branson sees second balloon trip, then maybe space.

text.p: British tycoon Richard Branson will have one more go at flying round the world by balloon and then give up dangerous adventures -- unless he has a chance to go into space.

Branson, 46, who had to abandon his first balloon circumnavigation attempt on Wednesday after less than 24 hours because of technical problems, told the Sun newspaper in an interview published on Saturday that his family wanted him to try again.
"I've discussed it with my family and they're behind me all the way," he said.
"This will be my last adventure -- unless I can get into space."
Branson's round-the-world bid ended prematurely with a dizzying descent into the Algerian desert less than 24 hours after taking off from Morocco.
The exact problem that caused the Virgin Global Challenger to plunge towards earth on Wednesday, with near-fatal results, is still not clear, but Branson described the balloon as a "test craft".

"Flying that particular balloon, I knew I was flying a test craft and there are obvious dangers in test flights," he told the Sun. "But this time we'll have the best designers ironing out the problems."

Branson, who made his name by developing the Virgin record company and now heads an airline bearing the same name, said people would never achieve anything if they worried all the time about what might go wrong.
"The thing about life is that you have to live it to the full," he said. "If someone dies doing something they love, then you can take comfort from that."
